title: Tal gives away his queen
summary: Varna, 1962: Tal lets his queen be trapped and wins with the pieces he gets in return.

steps.title: Varna, 1962
steps.text: By 1962 Mikhail Tal had already been world champion, and everyone knew his style: sacrifice first, let the opponent prove it was wrong later. At the chess Olympiad in Varna, Bulgaria, he faced the German master Hans-Joachim Hecht. In this game Tal walks his queen into a trap on purpose. Press play and find his moves.
steps.narration: Varna, 1962. Mikhail Tal against Hans-Joachim Hecht. Watch closely, because Tal is about to let his queen be trapped on purpose.

steps.title: Tal – Hecht, Varna Olympiad 1962
steps.text: White gets doubled pawns early but a big center. Then Tal brings his queen out to a4, where it can be trapped. He does not care: he is counting pieces and open lines, not points.
steps.narration: Tal brings his queen to the edge of the board, where it can be trapped. He knows. Find his moves.

notes.text: 8.bxc3: White has doubled pawns on the c-file, but the pawn mass in the center is strong.
15.Qa4+: the queen comes out with check. On a4 it is close to trouble.
17.Nc4: the knight heads for d6. Tal ignores that his bishop on h4 can be taken.
18...b5: Hecht traps the queen. It has no safe square left.
19...bxa4: the queen is gone. Tal has a knight and a monster pawn on f6 for it.
21.Bf5: the bishop hits Black's queen on e6. Hecht takes the h4 bishop first.
26.Bxa6: the smoke clears. Material is about level, but Tal's pieces are the active ones.
49.Rg5, after a long endgame Tal's extra activity tells. Black resigned.

guesses.prompt: The bishop on h4 is attacked, and ...b5 would trap the queen. What does Tal play?
guesses.hint: Do not save anything. Hit the knight on f6 with a pawn.
guesses.why: 18.e5! If ...b5 wins the queen, exf6 rips open the black king's side and the pawn heads for g7. Saving the bishop with Bg3 was also fine, but Tal wanted the fight.

guesses.prompt: The queen is gone. Which capture keeps Black busy?
guesses.hint: Your pawn on f6 can take on g7, and look at the rook on h8.
guesses.why: 20.fxg7 attacks the rook on h8 and puts a pawn one step from queening. Black must spend a move on ...Rg8.

guesses.prompt: Black just took your bishop on h4. Your bishop on f5 has a big target.
guesses.why: 22.Bxe6 takes the queen back. Tal has won his queen back with interest: the g7 pawn is still alive.

guesses.prompt: The bishop on a6 attacks your knight on c4. Answer with check.
guesses.hint: The knight can jump to a square next to the black king.
guesses.why: 23.Nd6+ moves the knight out of danger with check. Black never gets time to pick off White's loose pieces.

guesses.prompt: Black's king attacks the knight on d6 and his bishop eyes your rook on f1. One quiet move fixes both.
guesses.hint: Block the a6–f1 diagonal and fight that bishop at the same time.
guesses.why: 24.Bc4! The bishop leaves e6, blocks the diagonal to f1, and offers itself to the bishop on a6. Tal soon trades into an endgame where his pieces are the better ones.

steps.title: Why did it work?
steps.question: Tal let his queen be trapped on a4. Why was that not a disaster?

options.text: In return he got a knight, a pawn on g7 and an attack that won the queen back
options.why: Right. Every Black move was spent answering threats, and soon the queen came back on e6.

options.text: Hecht did not notice he could take the queen
options.why: He noticed and took it on move 19. It just did not help.

options.text: Queens are worth less than bishops
options.why: A queen is worth about nine pawns. Tal won it back with tactics, not because it was cheap.

steps.narration: Tal lost his queen and still won. Why?

steps.title: Count the whole position
steps.text: Tal did not ask "how many points do I have?" He asked "what can my pieces do?" When the queen fell, his pawn on g7, his knight and his bishops made threats every move, and the queen came back. A sacrifice works when the threats it creates are bigger than the material it gives.
steps.narration: A sacrifice works when it creates more threats than it gives away material. Tal counted threats, not points.
